newsitem.title: USA: Firearms sees operating income drop in FY98.
newsitem.headline: Firearms sees operating income drop in FY98.

text.p: Firearms Training Inc gave a warning to its shareholders late Thursday that operating income in its fiscal year 1998 could drop between 25 to 40 percent due to delays in U.S. military orders.
The company said revenue from U.S. military customers, however, was approximately $7 million below expectations in its fiscal first quarter of 1998.
In a statement, the company said the primary reason for lower than expected revenue during the quarter was the delay in expected follow-on orders from the U.S. Army National Guard.

The company anticipates that U.S. military revenue will be approximately $20 million to $25 million lower than previously expected in the full fiscal year ending March 31, 1998. The anticipated decrease in revenue of 13 percent to 18 percent for full fiscal 1998, as compared to fiscal 1997, primarily reflects revisions in the expected timing of business from the U.S. Army active and reserve components. This is expected to hurt fiscal 1998 operating margins, bringing them to roughly 20 to 25 percent, the company said.
